blocks.text: Ishta Devata Japa — Choosing Your Deity

runs.text: Ishta devata is your chosen beloved deity for daily worship. Family tradition, initiation, or inner calling guide the choice.
Japam lets you pick any playable deity on the menu grid for mantra japa.
Ask elders, respect kuladeivam, or follow the deity you feel drawn to in prayer. Stick with one ishta for steady vows unless your guru directs otherwise.

items: All Japam deities include mantra audio + count
Select ishta on Japam menu after sign-in or guest try
Combine with simple home lamp offering if desired

runs.text: The number 108 is one full round on a japa mala. Steady repetition calms the mind and deepens attention on the mantra’s meaning.
Some traditions prescribe 11 or 21 malas — ask your guru or priest for counts suited to your vow.

items: Chanting too fast and losing focus on the sound
Mixing multiple deity vows without guidance
Expecting only material results instead of bhakti and ethical living

runs.text: Home japa supports temple worship; it does not replace darshan. Visiting the temple on festival days or Saturdays strengthens family tradition.
Open Japam menu → choose ishta → play match-3 with mantra.

faqs.question: Can I change ishta often?
faqs.answer: Traditions prefer stability; change only with good reason or guru advice.

faqs.question: Multiple deities?
faqs.answer: Many honour Ganesha first then ishta; Japam supports per-deity modes.

faqs.question: Guru-hidden deities?
faqs.answer: Sai Baba and Bramhamgaaru are reserved in app — not in public play grid.

faqs.question: Need initiation?
faqs.answer: Mantra japa is open in many homes; diksha mantras need guru.

disclaimer.text: This article is for educational and devotional practice only. Japam does not provide medical, legal, or financial advice. Results depend on personal faith and consistent practice. Mantra text and audio in the app are for japa support; consult your family priest or tradition for formal puja rules.
